title: Family-based green card application (Form I-485): documents needed
use_when: The client is in the United States applying to adjust status on Form I-485 as an immediate relative or family preference immigrant.
note: Based on the USCIS Checklist of Required Initial Evidence for Form I-485 (page last reviewed 07/08/2025) and the Form I-485 Instructions (edition 09/18/26). The responsible lawyer decides what the matter needs.

i485-checklist.name: USCIS, Checklist of Required Initial Evidence for Form I-485 (for informational purposes only), immediate relatives and family-based preference section, last reviewed/updated 07/08/2025

i485-instr.name: USCIS, Instructions for Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, edition 09/18/26

situations.i130-filed-earlier: Was the Form I-130 filed earlier rather than together with this application?
situations.family-preference: Is the applicant in a family preference category rather than an immediate relative (spouse, parent or unmarried child under 21 of a U.S. citizen)?
situations.derivative: Is the applicant the spouse or unmarried child under 21 of a family preference principal applicant?
situations.prior-marriage: Is the applicant a derivative spouse where either party to the marriage was married before?
situations.k1-fiance: Did the applicant enter the United States as the fiance(e) of a U.S. citizen (K nonimmigrant)?
situations.arrests: Has the applicant ever been arrested, detained, charged or convicted anywhere in the world?
situations.j-visa: Has the applicant ever held J-1 or J-2 exchange visitor status?
situations.diplomatic-status: Does the applicant hold A, G, E or NATO nonimmigrant status?
situations.waiver-needed: Does the applicant need a waiver of a ground of inadmissibility?
situations.prior-removal: Does the applicant need permission to reapply for admission after deportation or removal?
situations.section-245i: Is the applicant applying under section 245(i)?
situations.foreign-language: Are any documents in a language other than English?

items.label: Two identical color passport-style photographs
items.detail: Taken recently. 2 by 2 inches, full face, frontal view, white to off-white background, printed on thin paper with a glossy finish, unmounted and unretouched.

items.label: Photocopy of a government-issued identity document with photograph
items.detail: For example, passport (even if expired), driver's license, or military identification document. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Photocopy of the birth certificate
items.detail: Issued by the appropriate civil authority from the country of birth; must list at least one parent. If unavailable or nonexistent, other acceptable evidence of birth such as church, school, or medical records, and proof of unavailability or nonexistence.

items.label: Evidence of inspection and admission or parole for the most recent arrival
items.detail: Copies, if available, of: passport page with admission or parole stamp (issued by a U.S. immigration officer); passport page with nonimmigrant visa; and Form I-94, Arrival/Departure Record. Not required for applicants under section 245(i). Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Copy of the approval or receipt notice (Form I-797) for the Form I-130 filed for the applicant
items.detail: Not needed when the Form I-485 is filed together with the Form I-130.

items.label: Evidence of continuously maintaining lawful status since arriving in the United States
items.detail: Copies such as: Form I-797 for all extensions of stay and changes of nonimmigrant status; Form I-94, including printouts of paperless I-94 admissions; Form I-20 or Form DS-2019 including all pages with notations by authorized officials; or passport page with an admission or parole stamp. Include evidence for every entry and for the time periods spent in the United States.

items.label: Exchange visitor (J-1 or J-2) documents
items.detail: Copies of all Forms IAP-66 and/or DS-2019 ever issued (if available), all available J-1 or J-2 visas, and all available Form I-94 records and passport pages with entry stamps showing admission in J status. If subject to the two-year foreign residence requirement: documentation of compliance, a granted waiver, or a favorable waiver recommendation letter from the Department of State.

items.label: Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record
items.detail: Signed by a civil surgeon. If required, it must be submitted with the Form I-485.

items.label: Form I-864 or I-864EZ, Affidavit of Support, from the sponsor
Evidence of a bona fide marriage to the U.S. citizen petitioner within 90 days after admission as a K nonimmigrant
Copy of documentation showing the relationship to the principal applicant
items.detail: Such as a marriage certificate, birth certificate, or adoption decree. If the marriage certificate is unavailable or does not exist, other acceptable evidence such as church records and proof of unavailability or nonexistence.

items.label: Copy of the approval or receipt notice (Form I-797) for the principal applicant's Form I-130
items.detail: Not needed when filing together with the principal applicant's Form I-485.

items.label: Evidence that any prior marriages legally ended
items.detail: Typically a divorce decree/certificate or death certificate.

items.label: Certified police and court records of all criminal charges, arrests, or convictions, regardless of final disposition
items.detail: An original or certified copy of the complete arrest report, plus as applicable: an official statement or court order showing the final disposition where no charges were filed; certified copies of the charging document and final disposition of each charge; any plea agreement; the probation or parole record or proof of completing the program; and a certified copy of any court order vacating, setting aside, sealing or expunging the record.

items.label: Form I-601, Application for Waiver of Grounds of Inadmissibility
Form I-212, Application for Permission to Reapply for Admission into the United States After Deportation or Removal
Form I-508, Waiver of Diplomatic Rights, Privileges, Exemptions, and Immunities
items.detail: If the applicant holds A, G, or E nonimmigrant status and has certain diplomatic privileges and immunities as a result of occupational status.

items.label: Form I-566, Interagency Record of Request
items.detail: Only if the applicant has A, G, or NATO nonimmigrant status.

items.label: Form I-485 Supplement A, Adjustment of Status Under Section 245(i)
Full English translation of every foreign-language document
items.detail: With a certification from the translator that the translation is complete and accurate and that they are competent to translate from the foreign language to English.
